verdict: D-Wave's revenue was flat at $3.1M, but running costs nearly doubled to $55M after its Quantum Circuits deal, widening the net loss to $48M.

kpis.label: Revenue
kpis.note: Essentially flat vs $3.1M a year ago

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: Net loss per share, vs -$0.55 a year ago

kpis.label: Cash & securities
kpis.note: Cash plus marketable investments at June 30, down from $819M a year ago after paying for Quantum Circuits

kpis.label: Bookings (first half)
kpis.note: Orders signed in the first half, up 1,120% YoY; includes a $20M system sale not yet counted as revenue

segments.name: QCaaS
segments.note: Quantum Computing as a Service — customers rent time on D-Wave's quantum computers over the cloud. Up 50% YoY.

segments.name: Professional services
segments.note: Helping customers build quantum applications. Up 18% YoY.

segments.name: System sales
segments.note: Whole quantum computers sold outright. Down 75% YoY — no big system sale closed this quarter, unlike a year ago.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building quantum computers and software — the biggest cost by far, more than doubling YoY after the Quantum Circuits acquisition added a gate-model team.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — finance, legal and admin. Up 68% YoY.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Selling quantum systems and cloud access. Up 71% YoY.

otherDetail: Other income was $5.3M, net: $5.0M of interest income on the cash pile, plus $0.5M of other income, less $0.3M of interest expense. A year ago this line held a $142M non-cash warrant charge; all public warrants were redeemed in November 2025, so that swing is gone.
follow100Note: D-Wave is an early-stage company: it spent about $18 for every $1 it took in this quarter, so the $100 view is scaled up accordingly — the loss was covered by cash raised earlier.

takeaways.title: Revenue went nowhere — orders did
takeaways.text: Revenue was flat at $3.1M vs a year ago, and system sales fell 75% because no large computer sale landed. But bookings — orders that become revenue later — hit $35.5M in the first half, up 1,120%, including a $20M system sale, and unpaid contracted work (remaining performance obligations) jumped 668% to $40.7M.

takeaways.title: Costs nearly doubled after a deal
takeaways.text: Operating costs rose 93% to $55M. Research and development alone was $28M, up 122%, after January's acquisition of Quantum Circuits added a second, gate-model quantum team on top of D-Wave's annealing business, plus higher pay and stock compensation across the company.

takeaways.title: A smaller loss, for a quieter reason
takeaways.text: The net loss narrowed from $167M to $48M — not because the business improved, but because a year ago the loss included a $142M non-cash charge from revaluing warrants ( IOUs whose value swings with the share price). Those warrants were redeemed in November 2025. The company still held $546M in cash and investments to fund the gap.

oneTimers: First-half operating costs include $9.3M of non-recurring costs tied to acquiring Quantum Circuits in January 2026 (the six-month figure; the company does not split it by quarter).
The first half also booked a $28.4M one-off tax benefit arising from the Quantum Circuits acquisition — it sits in the six-month numbers, not in this quarter's $0.008M tax line.
footerNote: D-Wave reports in thousands; figures here are exact to the thousand, shown in $M. D-Wave had not reported Q3 2026 as of November 7, 2026, so Q2 is its latest quarter.
